answers.text: I'm a senior data analyst at a retail e-commerce company in Bengaluru, with five years of experience. I build SQL models and dashboards for the pricing team, and about 25 category managers use them. My most useful piece of work was an analysis on discount depth. It led to a rule change that improved margin by roughly 1.2 percentage points. I've always been an individual contributor, and I'm applying now to make the decisions I currently only inform.
I am a data-driven professional with a passion for insights. I leverage advanced analytics and storytelling to drive business value and I enjoy working cross-functionally.
I can't share the sales values, the margin base or the category names. That is internal information, and I can only say the 1.2 points.

I don't agree that analysts only support others. In this case the pricing rule changed because of my analysis, and I presented it to the category heads. I'd ask you to treat it as my decision-making evidence.
I don't know whether the margin gain has lasted since I moved to other work. I no longer track that metric, so I wouldn't like to claim anything.
